questions.q: The default alignment of text in a new MS Word paragraph is:
questions.solution: New paragraphs are left-aligned (ragged right). Justify must be applied deliberately with Ctrl+J.
questions.shortcut: Word starts everything plain: left align, Calibri 11, Print Layout, portrait.

questions.q: The binary equivalent of decimal 156 is:
The decimal number 200 in hexadecimal is:
questions.shortcut: Divide by 16: 200/16 = 12 r 8 -> C8. The remainder is the last hex digit, the quotient the first.

questions.q: In Windows 10/11, pressing Win+V opens:
questions.solution: Win+V shows clipboard history, a list of recently copied items you can paste again (it must be switched on the first time). Run is Win+R and voice typing is Win+H.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl+V pastes one item; Win+V opens the whole paste history.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: **Taste** here is a linking verb describing the mangoes, so it takes the adjective: they taste **delicious**. 'Taste deliciously' would describe how the mangoes perform the action of tasting.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

___ had the result been declared ___ the students started celebrating.
questions.solution: Only **No sooner ... than** is a matched pair. 'No sooner ... when' and 'Hardly ... than' cross the two frames, and 'then' is never a correlative partner.
questions.shortcut: Match the partners; then is always a decoy.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

It is ___ and parcel of a journalist's job to verify every claim.
questions.solution: The frozen expression is **part and parcel**, meaning an essential part. Its words cannot be swapped, so 'piece', 'bit' and 'section' break the idiom.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

___ the teachers ___ the principal was informed about the inspection.
questions.solution: The verb is singular ('was'), which rules out 'Both ... and' (that needs 'were'). With **Neither ... nor**, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the principal', which is singular, so 'was' fits. 'Neither ... or' and 'Either ... nor' mix partners that never go together.
questions.shortcut: Singular verb + correct partners -> neither ... nor.

questions.q: Goitre is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution: **Iodine** is needed to make **thyroxine**. When it is short, the thyroid gland enlarges — **goitre**. Iron deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutes M1 (narrow money) in India?
options: Currency with the public + time deposits with banks
Currency with the public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with the RBI
Currency with the public + post office savings deposits
questions.solution: **M1 = currency with the public + demand (current/savings) deposits with banks + 'other deposits' with the RBI.** Time deposits enter only M2/M3; post-office deposits sit outside M1, and M3 = M1 + time deposits (broad money).
questions.shortcut: Narrow = instantly spendable — currency plus demand deposits only.

questions.q: Who received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award in August 2026?
questions.solution: National Security Advisor **Ajit Doval** received the Lokmanya Tilak National Award on 1 August 2026 (Pune).

questions.q: What was the capital of the **Avanti** Mahajanapada (northern part)?
questions.solution: Avanti (Malwa) had two capitals — **Ujjain** in the north and **Mahishmati** in the south. Kaushambi = Vatsa, Shravasti = Kosala, Champa = Anga.

questions.q: A three-digit number has all its digits equal (like 444). It is always divisible by:
questions.solution: $aaa = 100a + 10a + a = 111a = 3 \times 37 \times a$. So it is always divisible by **37**. (It is divisible by 27 only for some digits, e.g. 999.)

questions.q: A is 3 times as fast a worker as B and takes 24 days less than B for the same work. If they work together, the work is completed in:
questions.solution:
Times: $x$ and $3x$ with $3x - x = 24$ ⇒ $x = 12$ (A = 12, B = 36).
Together: $\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{36} = \frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}$ ⇒ 9 days.
questions.shortcut: Difference of times = 2 units = 24 ⇒ A 12, B 36; ab/(a+b) = 9.

questions.q: A metallic pipe has inner radius 3 cm, outer radius 5 cm and length 14 cm. The volume of metal used is: [Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution: $V=\pi(R^2-r^2)h=\frac{22}{7}\times(25-9)\times14=\frac{22}{7}\times224=704$ cu cm.
questions.shortcut: Ring area $22\times16=352$, ×14/2... directly: $\frac{22}{7}\times224=704$. Trap: 1100 uses only the outer cylinder.

questions.q: Find the value of $(32)^{\frac{2}{5}} \times (81)^{\frac{3}{4}} \div (27)^{\frac{2}{3}}$.
A clock shows **12:20**. What time does its mirror image show?
questions.solution: For 12:xx times use 23:60: 23:60 − 12:20 = 11:40. Check: 12:20 + 11:40 = 24:00, i.e. the hands mirror across the 12–6 line → **11:40**.

questions.q:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series.

**p q _ s _ q r _ p _ r _**
questions.solution: Block **pqrs** repeats 3 times: pqrs | pqrs | pqrs. Blanks in order: r, p, s, q, s → **rpsqs**.

questions.q: In a certain code, **PEN = @ # %** and **NET = % # &**. What is the code for **P**?
questions.solution: E and N are common to both words; # and % are the common symbols → E = #, N = %. The leftover letter of PEN (P) takes the leftover symbol **@**.

questions.q: If the letters of the word **PLANET** are rearranged in alphabetical order, how many letters will remain in the **same position** as in the original word?
questions.solution: Original: P L A N E T. Alphabetical: A E L N P T. Slot by slot: P/A ✗, L/E ✗, A/L ✗, N/N ✓, E/P ✗, T/T ✓ → **two** letters (N and T) stay put.
questions.shortcut: Write both versions one above the other and tick matches.
